title: Canonical recursive Project Filing System grammar
statement: Every governed repository MUST be a recursive tree of Modules. Each Module MUST contain README.md, contract.json, and at least one of code/ or mods/. Module roots and docs/ are closed. Project-defined Code MUST be flat unless a registered ecosystem profile owns mechanical namespace structure. Data and Info MUST be either flat or use the frozen role/[collection]/[part_000001] grammar at minimum necessary depth. Companion documentation presence and canonical naming/versioning MUST be complete.
rationale: One recursive filing grammar makes architectural containment physical, prevents hidden decomposition, distinguishes persisted inputs from derived outputs, permits mechanical ecosystem structure only through explicit profiles, scales human catalogs by collection, and removes arbitrary filesystem taxonomies.
failure_prevented: Unowned implementation islands, responsibility hidden beneath code, missing Module contracts, mixed flat/structured Elements, recursive data taxonomies, malformed version or partition folders, arbitrary documentation archives, unregistered ecosystem exceptions, and entropy-producing path aliases.
applicability: Every governed repository snapshot. Non-Fortress root artifacts and mechanical Code directories are admitted only by a validated Standard-owned ecosystem profile.
evaluation: The Fortress core compiles a deterministic Project Filing System model from stabilized paths and the validated ecosystem-profile registry; inventories every leaf; recursively validates Module and Element structure; enforces Code flatness, closed docs, Data/Info role-collection-partition depth, minimum necessary levels, _vN versions, part_000001 partitions, and companion documentation; then projects normalized violations into findings without adding leaf files to the CCG.

finding.message: An observed path or inferred Module violates the canonical recursive repository grammar.

remediation: Converge the path to the recursive Module grammar; keep source files directly beneath code unless a registered mechanical profile applies; retain only canonical companion docs; use the shallowest canonical Data/Info role and optional collection; use one part_000001-style physical partition level; and remove or register ecosystem-required root surfaces.
valid_example: A composite Module has README.md, contract.json, mods/, and docs/mods_docs.md; an atomic child has flat code/; a large dataset remains data/dataset/historical_events_v3/part_000001/... without creating volume-only Modules.
invalid_example: A scripts/ island exists at the root, code/parsing hides an architectural responsibility, docs/adr accumulates a private taxonomy, data/schema/schemas adds a redundant level, or info/report/reports/current recursively encodes informal states.
exception_policy: Only entries in the validated ecosystem filing-profile registry are exceptions. Profiles may admit exact root/Element filenames or mechanically required Code namespace trees; repository-specific prose and arbitrary directory names cannot create exemptions.
history: Introduced during CHG-REPOSITORY-GRAMMAR-0007 as the canonical replacement for the earlier project-declared placement model.
Extended to require one Module contract and bidirectional mods_docs.md decomposition documentation.
Recognizes root .gitattributes as Git-supported integration authority needed to preserve canonical LF contract bytes across platforms.

Finalized as the Project Filing System grammar with profile-owned ecosystem surfaces, flat Code, closed Docs, frozen Data/Info roles, one collection and partition level, _vN versions, and scalable machine inventory.
